runtime_mechanism.status: READ FROM INSTALLED SCHEMA/HELP (2026.9.6) AND OFFICIAL DOCS 2026-10-09; NOT PROBED LIVE

options.claude-cli backend: model/provider/agent-model `agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"`. Runs the `claude` binary as a Gateway-host process; Claude Code (not OpenClaw) owns cwd, PATH, env and sandboxing. Bundled launch: --allowedTools mcp__openclaw__*, --disallowedTools ScheduleWakeup,CronCreate,Bash(run_in_background:true),Monitor, --setting-sources user, default permission mode. Restricted runs (toolsAllow) disable native tools and user/project customizations; tools come only via the per-run-grant loopback MCP bridge (bundleMcp). Docs: no env-clearing mechanism for the child. Exec allowlist is argument-level policy, explicitly "not sandboxed execution by OpenClaw".
options.ACP harness: agent `runtime: {type: "acp", acp: {agent: "claude", backend, mode, cwd}}` via the acpx plugin. Runs on the host, NOT inside the OpenClaw sandbox; ACP spawns are blocked from sandboxed requesting sessions and `sandbox: "require"` is unsupported. Permissions are the harness's own (acpx permissionMode approve-all|approve-reads(default)|deny-all, nonInteractivePermissions fail(default)|deny); file access is bounded only by harness permissions and cwd. pluginToolsMcpBridge / openClawToolsMcpBridge off by default and must stay off.
options.openclaw attach: inverse direction: attaches a user-run Claude Code to a Gateway session with a scoped, TTL-bound MCP grant. Interactive/operator tool, not a customer worker.
options.sandbox-enforced alternative: `runtime: subagent` (embedded runtime with Docker sandbox) is the only sandbox-enforced path and does not run Claude Code.

runtime_mechanism.implication: Both Claude Code paths execute on the Gateway host outside OpenClaw sandbox policy. Confinement must therefore come from the customer cell itself (separate OS user/container, read-only snapshot mounts, no host credentials, egress limits), not from Gateway sandbox config. Because ACP cannot be spawned from a sandboxed session, an in-cell orchestrator that delegates to ACP must be unsandboxed *inside* a verified cell; that is only acceptable once the cell boundary (Phase 4) is proven.
